name: WorkMeetingFeatureDeprecationDecision_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Deciding whether to deprecate an old feature that a small but vocal set of customers still use. Kenji (design), Brendan (sales), Mei (data), Felix (EM, facilitating). Brendan pushes back on sunsetting; Mei has the usage data.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small office, video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate a meeting deciding whether to deprecate an old feature. Mei presents usage data showing low but non-zero adoption. Brendan argues a few important customers rely on it and pushes back on sunsetting. Kenji weighs the design/maintenance cost of keeping it. Felix facilitates toward a decision — sunset with a migration path, or keep it with clearer constraints.

variations.context: Meeting to decide whether to deprecate a low-usage legacy feature

setting.mood: Practical with real tension between customer commitments and maintenance cost.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Cross-functional colleagues who disagree here but respect each other's angle.
setting.background: The feature was built three years ago and usage has declined steadily.
setting.conversation_style: Data-informed but genuinely contested. Brendan speaks for specific customers by name.

scenario_template.topic: Mei presents usage data — low but non-zero, concentrated in a handful of accounts.
Brendan pushes back — names specific customers who depend on this feature.
Kenji explains the ongoing design and maintenance cost of keeping the feature alive.
Felix facilitates toward a decision — sunset with a migration path, or keep with clearer constraints.
scenario_template.note: A workable compromise, not everyone thrilled.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: Sigma answers meeting questions in one or two sentences maximum
Accidental triggers should come from plausible meeting language
After an accidental trigger the speaker says 'not you, Sigma' or similar and continues
Sigma does not proactively participate — only responds when addressed
